- When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.27) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% relative to prior period.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior day), model often overshoots and fails to correct; cap forecast at +3% above prior peak for next 3–5 days.
- If sentiment shows strong bullish momentum (e.g., 0.80+ for 3+ consecutive days), model tends to overreact; apply downward bias of 1–2% to forecast if price is rising.
- Model underestimates when sentiment is neutral or mildly bearish (0.27–0.53) and price is trending downward; adjust forecast upward by 0.5–1.5% to match sentiment drift.
- For 30-day horizon, model often fails to capture mean reversion; if price has deviated >2% from 14-day moving average, apply correction toward average with 1–2% decay per day.
- When sentiment is volatile (alternating 0.27/0.80), model overfits short-term noise; smooth forecast by averaging last 3–5 days’ values before applying sentiment-weighted adjustment.
